Found this browsing /new...What am I listening to? What's ASMR? I know what it says int he sidebar, but I feel this subverse could benefit from a sticky because Autonomous Sensory Meridian Response doesn't tell me anything.

I don't know if anyone is maintaining this subverse. I'll link you to some information, but if you have specific questions or concerns I'm willing to try helping you myself.

  • http://www.asmrlab.com/
  • https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_sensory_meridian_response
  • http://www.vice.com/read/asmr-the-good-feeling-no-one-can-explain

When reading about ASMR, you'll find that some people use the words like orgasm or drug to describe what they are experiencing. These words are not to be taken literally in the context of ASMR, they are only used for the sake of comparison. To give you some idea of why ASMR is difficult to explain, consider how you might describe enjoying chocolate ice cream, or Mozart. People who have never had such an experience will not have the common reference point required to understand it.

Lastly, stay away from the comments sections of YouTube ASMR videos. They are full of unhelpful, crude remarks which will not improve your understanding. That's generally true with all YouTube videos, but even more so in this case.

HTH
